field_19_fines.what: The Field, study 19, 'The fine for working', fines.tsv: per warned US tornado 2008-2023 (10,540), year, state, rating, injuries, deaths, and a logistic model's harm probability without the warning (p) and with it (q), for anyone hurt (H) and anyone killed (D)
field_19_fines.committed: no; the columns used are carried in data.js, rounded to six places, with attribution
field_19_fines.used: p for both outcomes and the harm flags; q recomputed from p and the odds ratio and checked against the Field's q

field_19_results.what: The Field, study 19, results.json: the fitted odds ratios of a warning and their 95 % intervals
field_19_results.used: OR 0.6801 (0.589-0.782) for harm, 0.8788 (0.643-1.210) for death; event counts 798 and 227

holland_1986.what: Paul W. Holland, 'Statistics and Causal Inference', Journal of the American Statistical Association 81(396), 1986, 945-960
holland_1986.used: p. 947: the statement of the Fundamental Problem of Causal Inference (short quotation), and the 'statistical solution' that replaces the unit's effect by its average over a population (paraphrased)

atelier_c008.what: The Atelier, cycle 008 presentation, The Heeded Column: the refutation condition this page tests
